_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::mixture#1. The advice (make the fibre direction per-element rather than uniform) holds, but FIBER_VEC is not a 4C key: adding it to ELAST_CoupAnisoExpo on upstream mixture_elast_hyper_dynamic.4C.yaml is a parse abort, 'Could not match this input' from global_data/4C_global_data_read.cpp. The real mechanism is the integer INIT on the anisotropic summand plus FIBER1 on the element line: INIT: 1 with no element fibres gives 'Could not find element coordinate system or element fibers!' from mat/4C_mat_anisotropy_extension_default.cpp, and INIT: 1 with FIBER1 written on every element line runs and changes all six result tests — the fibre direction is genuinely per-element data that moves the answer. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: Could not find element coordinate system or element fibers!

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the FIBER_VEC arm: do not inject the invented key. The material parses, EXIT_FIBERVEC becomes 0 and the parse diagnostic vanishes, so the fixture must go red.

remove the pathology from the INIT arms: leave INIT at the angle-based mode. The element-fibre diagnostic vanishes, the per-element arm no longer changes the answer, and both EXIT codes go to 0, so the fixture must go red.
